name: Aspen Meadows Resort
positioning: All-suite resort on the 40-acre Aspen Institute campus, designed by Bauhaus artist Herbert Bayer, within walking distance of Aspen
best_for: Art and design lovers drawn to Herbert Bayer's Bauhaus campus
Skiers and active travelers who want suites near Aspen's mountains
Families who want suites with separate living and sleeping areas

facts.text: The resort is rooted in the history of the Aspen Institute and was designed by Herbert Bayer.
The grounds cover 40 acres of rolling meadows and groves.
The resort is within walking distance of Aspen's outdoor pursuits, skiing, shopping and restaurants.
All accommodations are suites, inspired by the resort's Bauhaus roots.
The guest suites feature floor-to-ceiling windows and contemporary furnishings.
Every suite has living, working and sleeping areas, suiting everyone from business travelers to families.
The junior suites include Ferenc Berko photographs and a drop station for gear and jackets.
The Health Center has TRX, cardio and weight equipment, a Peloton bike, steam rooms, an outdoor heated saline lap pool, a hot tub and a half-court indoor gym with basketball.
The Racquet Sports Center, in partnership with Brisas, has a padel court, a petanque court, backgammon tables and a lounge.
Guests have a complimentary ski shuttle to Buttermilk.
Through a partnership with Ski Butlers, ski rentals are delivered to all four mountains or directly to the resort.
The West End Social restaurant has 270-degree views of Aspen's mountains.

highlights.text: The entire 40-acre property was designed by Herbert Bayer between 1953 and 1973 and is considered a Bauhaus-inspired total work of art.
The campus includes three art galleries and many Bayer-designed outdoor sculptures, including Anaconda, Marble Garden and Kaleidoscreen, along with the earthworks of Anderson Park.
Bayer's Grass Mound, completed in 1955, is one of the first earthworks ever made, predating the land art movement by nearly ten years.
Andy Goldsworthy's Stone River, a serpentine sandstone wall, winds into and through the campus's Doerr-Hosier Center.
Visitors can sign up for complimentary guided walking tours led by landscape architect Ann Mullins.

considerations.text: A private patio or balcony comes with most guest suites, not all of them.
The outdoor heated lap pool must be reserved; the hot tub is first-come, first-served.
